_note: Synthetic demo messages created for the UniPods Pulse demo. No real person wrote any of these.

messages.author: Amara Obi
messages.text: Announcement: registration for the UniPods Hackathon 2026 is now open. Sign up in the portal before you form a team.

messages.author: Chidi Nwosu
messages.text: Just registered. Is there a limit on team size this year?

messages.author: Tunde Bello
messages.text: Two to five people per team. It was four last year, they raised it.

messages.author: Ngozi Eze
messages.text: Looking for one more person for our team. We are working on the AI track and we need someone comfortable with backend work.

messages.author: Kelechi Anyanwu
messages.text: I can join, I do mostly TypeScript and Postgres. Sending you a message.

messages.author: Ngozi Eze
messages.text: Perfect, that gives us four. We still have room for one more if anyone is looking.

messages.author: Fatima Sule
messages.text: What is the deadline for declaring teams? I saw the eighteenth somewhere in the draft schedule.

messages.author: Tunde Bello
messages.text: The draft I have says team declarations close on September 18. Someone should confirm with the organisers because I have seen two different dates.

messages.author: Chidi Nwosu
messages.text: Yes please confirm, our whole plan depends on whether we have one extra day.

messages.author: Amara Obi
messages.text: Announcement: mentor office hours run every day from 16:00 to 18:00 WAT in the community call room. Outside those hours, post technical questions in build-help.

messages.author: Kelechi Anyanwu
messages.text: Does the AI track require us to host our own vector database, or can we use a managed one?

messages.author: Tunde Bello
messages.text: The brief does not say. It only requires that private community data stays on infrastructure you control and is deleted after demo day.

messages.author: Ngozi Eze
messages.text: We are running Postgres with pgvector so that the data never leaves our own database. It is one fewer thing to explain to the judges.

messages.author: Fatima Sule
messages.text: Is there a template for the submission README?

messages.author: Chidi Nwosu
messages.text: Not that I have seen. The guidelines just list what has to be in it: repository link, README, three-minute demo video, and every member with their role.

messages.author: Kelechi Anyanwu
messages.text: Reminder to everyone on our team: the demo video is not optional. Submissions without one are disqualified.

messages.author: Ngozi Eze
messages.text: How are people handling chat messages in retrieval? Individual messages are too short to match anything useful.

messages.author: Tunde Bello
messages.text: We group consecutive messages from the same channel into a window and embed the window. A single line like "agreed" carries no meaning on its own.

messages.author: Kelechi Anyanwu
messages.text: Same here. We also keep the author and the date inside the embedded text so questions about who said what can retrieve.

messages.author: Fatima Sule
messages.text: Did anyone write down what was decided in the AI architecture session? I could not attend.

messages.author: Chidi Nwosu
messages.text: The recording is being uploaded. Short version: hybrid retrieval, not fine-tuning, and every answer has to cite its sources.

messages.author: Amara Obi
messages.text: Announcement and correction: team declarations are due Thursday, September 17, 2026, by close of business. An earlier draft schedule said September 18. The seventeenth is the correct date. Please declare your team before then.

messages.author: Tunde Bello
messages.text: Thanks for the correction, we were working from the eighteenth. Declaring ours today.

messages.author: Ngozi Eze
messages.text: Declared. Four members, AI track, project is a community knowledge assistant.

messages.author: Amara Obi
messages.text: Announcement: the AI Challenge Brief has been uploaded to the resource library. Read the evaluation notes carefully, especially the part about unanswerable questions.

messages.author: Fatima Sule
messages.text: Our extraction keeps losing page numbers on PDFs, which makes citations useless. Has anyone solved that?

messages.author: Kelechi Anyanwu
messages.text: You have to capture text per page rather than taking the whole document string, then carry the page number through chunking as metadata.

messages.author: Chidi Nwosu
messages.text: Compute credits are capped at 100 USD per member per term, so plan your embedding runs. Re-embedding the whole archive repeatedly will burn through it.

messages.author: Ngozi Eze
messages.text: Has anyone heard when the judging panel is announced? I cannot find it in the guidelines.

messages.author: Fatima Sule
messages.text: Not in anything I have read either. Might be worth asking at office hours today.
